source_user: Define tensor parallelism and explain one reason it matters in LLM infrastructure. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: Tensor parallelism (TP) partitions selected layer weights or activations across devices so each rank computes a shard of an operation, then communicates partial results with a collective such as all-reduce or all-gather. It matters because the partition can reduce per-device parameter, activation, or temporary memory and let a layer fit across devices, at the cost of synchronization and interconnect traffic. Mechanism: a sharded matrix multiply produces rank-local partial outputs that are combined according to the layout. Boundary: extra TP ranks are not automatically faster; small matrices, short sequences, an imbalanced partition, or a slow/contended fabric can make collective time dominate. State layer dimensions, batch and sequence units, precision, topology, TP degree, and measure compute, collective, memory, throughput, latency, and output correctness before generalizing.

Aggregate memory capacity or utilization can conceal per-rank OOM, imbalance, or latency regressions.
